key_insight: Code2Video guides video generation with agent-authored 3D proxies, making scene structure and motion explicitly controllable. The reported findings suggest that proxy design should match the task: coarse proxies favor natural motion, while the provided abstract does not complete the comparison with medium-granularity proxies.
problem_solved: How to choose 3D proxy detail, physics simulation, and prompts to improve generated video quality—and understand the strengths and limits of code-guided video generation.
method: Use agent-authored 3D proxies to guide video structure and dynamics.
Run controlled experiments varying proxy granularity, physics simulation, and prompting.
Assess generated videos through blinded human evaluation to identify task-dependent trade-offs.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the study suggests that more detailed proxies are not automatically better: coarse proxies can support more natural motion. Its evaluation approach helps inform task-specific choices, although the supplied abstract is incomplete.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: agent-authored code → 3D proxy → generated video.
Side-by-side proxy examples showing coarse, medium, and fine scene detail.
Comparison strip pairing proxy animations with generated video frames.
Evaluation panel illustrating physics and prompting variations alongside blinded human ratings.
paper_title: Coda-DaVinci: Reimagining Video Generation with Code2Video
paper_authors: Yiyan Ji, Qixun Wang, Yang Shi, Zhuoran Zhang, Yifan Xu
